newsitem.title: UK: BOE's Foot warns banks over lending standards.
newsitem.headline: BOE's Foot warns banks over lending standards.

text.p: Bank of England executive director Michael Foot on Thursday warned commercial banks not to lower their guard on lending standards despite the lure of an environment currently perceived as benign.

"It is exactly at such good points in the lending cycle in the past that credit officers begin to think that "it is always going to be like this' or, in the worst cases, that they can walk on water," Foot said in a speech to credit risk managers.
Foot also cautioned that lending to larger corporates or countries should be treated with extra care as it is less susceptible to statistical analysis than consumer loans.

For this type of lending, Foot, who deals with supervision and surveillance of the banking system, said banks should resist cutting margins purely on competitive grounds and should not sacrifice covenants which give lenders the opportunity to intervene in the affairs of the borrower.
He also says that banks should not be influenced by every shift of sentiment in what is the "hot" place, product or industry to back.

"One excellent discipline here is regularly to ask yourself why you think you know more about the economic risks of mandate X then your competitors," Foot said. "No satisfactory answer to this very basic question maybe means you don't want the mandate after all!"
Foot extols the merits of diversification in a loan book but warns that this will inevitably lead to ventures in new areas of business and/or new products.

"The same maxim still applies; you must know enough about the risks you are buying to feel comfortable that the price adequately reflects those risks," Foot added., "Asset acquisition for its own sake is not sensible. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717.
